text: 79 Guidance for national tuberculosis programmes on the management of tuberculosis in children Roles and responsibilities of health workers at various levels of the health system Health workers at all levels of care (including primary care staff, general clinicians and paediatricians in public and private health care facilities) have potential roles in, and responsibilities for, ensuring comprehensive and coordinated care for a child with TB or a child who is a TB contact. Health workers at all levels need to be aware of their responsibilities to ensure that all children treated for TB are registered with the NTP. Box 3 provides examples of the tasks of health workers at various levels of health care. Box 3. Tasks of health workers at the various levels of health care Primary care level l Identify children with symptoms and signs suggestive of TB as well as contacts of newly diagnosed source cases (usually adults with sputum smear-positive PTB) l Refer sick child to first referral level of care as appropriate l In line with NTP guidelines, arrange treatment or referral of children l Identify child contacts with no evidence of TB disease who require IPT l Arrange follow-up for children who are being treated for TB or with IPT l Refer in the case of treatment failure l Provide HIV counselling and testing l Arrange follow-up for HIV-related care l Arrange family-centred care, including nutritional support l Identify source case and screen close contacts for any child diagnosed with TB l Ensure registration of all children treated for TB with the district NTP office First referral level l Make a diagnosis of TB disease or infection with M. tuberculosis l Start treatment for TB and for HIV when indicated l Identify source case and screen close contacts for any child diagnosed with TB l Ensure registration of all children treated for TB with the district NTP office l Refer the child back to the primary care level and/or appropriate health care worker for ongoing treatment and follow-up l Provide inpatient care as appropriate, including nutritional support l Manage common side-effects l Refer child to second care level in case of severe or complicated TB l Refer child to second care level in case of diagnostic uncertainty l Refer child to second care level in case of treatment failure l Refer child to second care level in case of suspected DR-TB and MDR-TB Second referral level l Diagnose and manage complicated TB, including most cases of disseminated TB, tuberculous meningitis and MDR-TB in children l Identify source case and screen close contacts for any child diagnosed with TB l Advise the NTP on the management of complicated TB cases l Ensure registration of all children treated for TB with the district NTP office l Refer the child back to the primary or secondary care level and/or appropriate health care worker for ongoing treatment and follow-up
